question: The SI unit of luminous intensity is
solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**The SI Unit of Luminous Intensity:**

__
 
• Luminous intensity is a measure of the wavelength-weighted power emitted by a light source in a particular direction, per unit solid angle. It quantifies how bright a light source appears to the human eye. The SI unit for luminous intensity is the **candela (cd)**.
 
• The candela is one of the seven base units in the International System of Units (SI). It is defined by the intensity of light emitted in a particular direction by a source that produces monochromatic radiation of frequency 540 × 10¹² hertz, with a radiant intensity of 1/683 watt per steradian.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

**Option 1: Watt**

 
• The watt (W) is the SI unit of power, which measures the rate at which energy is transferred or converted. It is defined as one joule per second. While luminous intensity and power are related concepts, they are not the same. Luminous intensity specifically accounts for the sensitivity of the human eye to different wavelengths of light, whereas power is a more general measure of energy transfer.

**Option 2: Mol**

 
• The mole (mol) is the SI unit of the amount of substance. It quantifies the number of elementary entities (such as atoms, molecules, or ions) in a given sample.

**Option 3: Meter**

 
• The meter (m) is the SI unit of length. It measures the distance between two points in space.
